title: Measuring with console.time Check
description: Use timing habits that support Big-O intuitions.

options.text: Elapsed time for this machine, this input, this run

questions.explanation: Big-O predicts growth; `console.time` measures this machine, this input, this run. Treat microbenchmarks with skepticism.

questions.prompt: A good timing habit is to:

options.text: Warm up once, use large enough `n`, and compare ratios as `n` grows
Always open DevTools while measuring for accuracy
Trust a single run as definitive proof

questions.explanation: Warm up (JIT / caches), use large enough `n`, same environment, and compare ratios as `n` grows — one run is an anecdote.

questions.prompt: If doubling `n` roughly doubles time, that pattern matches:
questions.explanation: Compare ratios as `n` grows — does doubling `n` roughly double time? That matches `O(n)`.

questions.prompt: For finer control in Node than `console.time`, the lesson points to:
questions.explanation: For finer control in Node, `performance.now()` from `node:perf_hooks` avoids `console` formatting overhead.
